sense: a certain one or number, not named

terms.grammar: adjective; plural aliquī, aliquae, aliqua; the pronoun is aliquis, aliquid
evidence: Plin. Ep. 3.5.10: ut nōn aliquā parte prōdesset
Cic. Fin. 5.5: in aliquā historiā vestīgium pōnimus
terms.comment: A thing or person that exists, though it does not matter which (Lewis & Short s.v. aliquis; see someone, something). After sī, nisi, num, nē it loses its ali- (see any). English “some” before a mass noun (“some bread”) is usually left out in Latin, or said with paulum (see a little).

terms.gloss: some, a certain (known but not named)
evidence: Mart. 1.16.1: sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediōcria
terms.comment: In the plural, “some” set against others: sunt quaedam mediōcria, some are middling.

terms.grammar: adjective, mostly plural; also written apart, nōn nūllī
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.146: vīna nōn nūllī Graeca (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BC 1.13.4: nōnnūlla pars mīlitum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. aliquot): nōnnūllī picks out an indefinite number from among several, “some of them”; aliquot is a small number (see several).

evidence: Caes. BG 3.25: cum aliī fossās complērent, aliī dēfēnsōrēs vallō dēpellerent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Some … others … others”: each group gets its own aliī; the last may be nōnnūllī or pars (Lewis & Short s.v. alius).

phrases.latin: dīcere etiam solēbat nūllum esse librum tam malum ut nōn aliquā parte prōdesset
phrases.english: he used to say, too, that no book was so bad as not to be useful in some part

phrases.latin: aestātis mīra clēmentia: semper āēr spīritū aliquō movētur
phrases.english: the summer is wonderfully mild: the air is always stirred by some breeze

phrases.latin: quācumque enim ingredimur, in aliquā historiā vestīgium pōnimus
phrases.english: for wherever we walk, we set foot on some piece of history

phrases.latin: sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediōcria, sunt mala plūra quae legis hīc
phrases.english: some of what you read here is good, some middling, more of it bad

phrases.latin: prōferēbant aliī purpuram, tūs aliī, gemmās aliī, vīna nōn nūllī Graeca
phrases.english: some brought out purple cloth, others incense, others jewels, some Greek wines

phrases.latin: ex quō mihi inter virtūtēs grammaticī habēbitur aliqua nescīre
phrases.english: so I shall count it among a teacher’s virtues not to know some things

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
